title: Curtain Falling

patient.name: Mr Darren Loh Wei Jie
patient.presenting_complaint: Sudden increase in floaters and a dark shadow at the bottom of vision in the right eye since this morning

history.hpc: Mr Loh woke up this morning with a dramatic increase in floaters in the right eye — he describes a 'cobweb' and several new black dots. He has also noticed a dark curtain rising from the bottom of his vision that has progressed over the past 6 hours to cover the inferior half of his visual field. He denies any trauma. He had a brief episode of flashing lights in the same eye 2 weeks ago which he ignored. He is a high myope and has worn glasses since age 8.
history.pmhx: Nil significant, no previous eye surgery or laser treatment
history.social_hx: Non-smoker, occasional alcohol, works long hours at a computer, physically active — recently started a gym programme

examination_findings.anterior_segment: Right: clear cornea, no cells in anterior chamber, tobacco dust (pigment cells) visible in anterior vitreous — Shafer's sign. Left: clear.

fundus.right: Bullous inferior retinal detachment extending from 4 o'clock to 8 o'clock, reaching posterior pole — macula appears to be off (flat foveal reflex absent). Vitreous haemorrhage obscuring superior periphery. Horseshoe tear visible at 7 o'clock with rolled posterior flap.
fundus.left: High myopic fundus — tessellated appearance, peripapillary atrophy, lattice degeneration at 6 o'clock — no detachment

investigations.b_scan_ultrasound: Right: bullous retinal detachment confirmed on B-scan, mobile membrane with aftermovement. Vitreous haemorrhage present.
investigations.visual_field: Right: superior visual field loss corresponding to inferior detachment

diagnosis: Rhegmatogenous retinal detachment (RRD), right eye, macula-off, caused by horseshoe tear at 7 o'clock. High myopia is the predisposing factor.

immediate: Urgent same-day surgical referral — macula-off RRD requires emergency surgery within 24 hours
Nil by mouth from midnight — prepare for theatre
Advise patient to lie supine with head down to shift fluid away from macula (positional therapy — limited evidence but low risk)
Surgical options: pars plana vitrectomy (PPV) with gas tamponade, or scleral buckle, or combined
follow_up: Postoperative: face-down positioning if gas tamponade used (SF6 or C3F8), avoid flying until gas resorbs
Review at 1 day, 1 week, 1 month post-op for retinal re-attachment and IOP monitoring
Visual prognosis: guarded — macula-off RRDs have variable recovery, may take months
Left eye: treat lattice degeneration with prophylactic laser retinopexy
Annual dilated fundus exam both eyes indefinitely
patient_education: This is a surgical emergency — delay worsens prognosis significantly
High myopia increases lifetime risk of retinal tears and detachment
Any new floaters, flashes, or field loss in the other eye requires immediate emergency review
After gas surgery: no flying, no high altitude travel until gas bubble resolves (4–8 weeks)

key_points: Elicits onset and progression of the shadow/curtain — direction and rate of spread
Asks about preceding flashes (photopsia) and floaters — signs of PVD
High myopia history — major risk factor
Prior episodes of flashes 2 weeks ago — missed warning sign
Requests dilated fundus examination to identify tears and extent of detachment
B-scan ultrasound if vitreous haemorrhage obscures view
Checks IOP — low IOP is a clue for RD
Examines fellow eye for lattice degeneration and risk assessment
Correctly identifies rhegmatogenous retinal detachment (not exudative or tractional)
Identifies macula involvement — macula-off vs on changes urgency and prognosis
Names appropriate surgical option (PPV or scleral buckle)
Post-operative care: positioning, no flying with gas
Prophylactic treatment of fellow eye for lattice degeneration
